join_order.notes: Single 113-row scan resolves it_genres and it_votes; also resolve g_m from name.gender dict.

join_order.build: genre_name_set (6 string_views: Horror, Action, Sci-Fi, Thriller, Crime, War)
join_order.notes: Use movie_info__info_type_id CSR to iterate only rows where info_type_id==it_genres (~hundreds of K to few M rows), then varlen length-prune + equality check against 6-entry hash set. Collect movie_ids into set T.
For each mv in T, lookup mi_idx range and find row where info_type_id==it_votes; capture mi_idx.info for MIN.

join_order.probe: cast_info (via cast_info__movie_id offsets, only for mv that passed votes probe)
join_order.notes: For each mv that has votes, probe ci range, test note IN writer-set AND n_gender[person_id-1]==g_m. Any hit qualifies the movie.

data_structures.movie_set_T: absl::flat_hash_set<int32_t> or sorted vector<int32_t> (expected ~hundreds of K)
data_structures.aggregation: three scalar MIN accumulators (string_view + materialize on update)

parallelism.notes: Parallelize CSR scan of movie_info genres rows into thread-local T sets, then merge. Parallelize probe loop over T across 12 threads with thread-local MIN aggregates, final reduce.

indexes.purpose: iterate only mi rows with info_type_id==it_genres
join_lookup for writer cast per movie
